{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In mathematics, a '''Hartshorne ellipse''' is an [[ellipse]] in the [[unit ball]] bounded by the [[4-sphere]] '''S'''<sup>4</sup> such that the ellipse and the circle given by intersection of its plane with '''S'''<sup>4</sup> satisfy the [[Poncelet condition]] that there is a triangle with vertices on the circle and edges tangent to the ellipse. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Hartshorne|authorlink=Robin Hartshorne|year=1978}}, who showed  that they correspond to  ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 [[instantons]] on '''S'''<sup>4</sup>.
